data.narrative:
SpaceX operates in Space & Aerospace as a public-stage company. The valuation universe comprises 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including Rocket Lab, Planet Labs, Firefly Aerospace, and Astroscale, spanning a wide maturity spectrum within the sector.

Peer-median methodology was the applicable triangulation approach. Across four same-sector, same-stage comparables, the median valuation is $5.2B, with a range spanning $840M (Astroscale) to $40.0B (Rocket Lab). This wide dispersion reflects material heterogeneity in business models, launch cadence, and revenue maturity within commercial spaceflight. Public-comp anchoring using sector P/S multiples (24.4x median across six tickers) could not be applied due to absence of disclosed revenue figures for the target.

The analysis supports a triangulated valuation range of $4.4B to $6.0B, centered on the peer median of $5.2B. Key uncertainties include revenue composition between launch services, satellite operations, and government contracts, which drive material valuation dispersion within the peer set. The $40B outlier (Rocket Lab) suggests upside if SpaceX commands a premium multiple, though the analysis provides no basis to quantify such adjustment. Given single-method reliance, confidence in point estimates remains constrained; wider sensitivity bounds are warranted for investment decision-making.
